Every server enforces these policies on mesh traffic -- what it relays between nodes, what reaches it and what it sends. The first policy that matches a packet decides; what none matches is dropped. Replies always pass. Internet traffic through an exit is not mesh traffic, and spokes keep their own firewall.

#NameActionFromToServices
1smballowgroup:laptopsnode:nastcp/445
2allow-all
Every mesh address		allowanyanyany

Add a policy

From, To and members take references -- zone:NAME (policies only), node:NAME, containers:NAME (a node's container network), group:NAME, role:server, role:spoke, role:phone, addr:NAME -- and addresses: 10.77.1.5, 10.77.1.0/24, 10.77.1.5-10.77.1.20. Services take svc:NAME, tcp/22, udp/1000-2000, tcp (every port) and icmp (ping). Separate entries with commas; empty is any.

What every server enforces

The system rules keep the mesh working and no policy changes them; after the policies, each zone allows traffic within it unless it says deny; then the rest is dropped.

  1. allow any -> any icmp (system: ping)
  2. allow 10.77.2.1 -> 10.77.1.1 tcp/445 (policy: smb)
  3. allow any -> any any (policy: allow-all)
  4. drop everything else
